en: I'm going to study tonight.
note: Future plan: conjugate ir + a + infinitive. Voy a estudiar uses the yo form voy.

en: You're going to learn a lot. (one person)
note: Tú takes vas in ir a + infinitive. The second verb stays aprender.

en: He's going to call tomorrow.
note: Él takes va. Keep the a between va and llamar.

en: She's going to arrive soon.
note: Ella takes va, just like él. Pronto means soon.

en: We're going to eat at home.
es: Nosotros vamos a comer en casa.
note: Nosotros takes vamos. Vamos a comer expresses a future plan in this sentence.

en: They're going to travel next month.
es: Ellos van a viajar el próximo mes.
note: Ellos takes van. El próximo mes means next month.

en: You're going to like this place. (plural)
es: A ustedes les va a gustar este lugar.
note: Este lugar is the singular subject of gustar, so use va. Les identifies the people who will like it.

en: I'm going to buy bread.
note: Only ir changes for the subject in this future pattern; comprar remains an infinitive.

en: I'm not going to work tomorrow.
note: Put no before voy to make the whole future plan negative.

en: Are you going to come with me? (one person)
note: The future question uses vas a + infinitive. Conmigo means with me.

en: What are we going to do?
note: Qué introduces what. Vamos identifies we, so nosotros is unnecessary.

en: Where are you going to stay? (plural)
note: Quedarse uses se with ustedes. Se van a quedar and van a quedarse are both valid.

en: I'm going to rest for a while.
note: Un rato means a while. Voy a + infinitive is common for everyday plans.

en: She's going to make dinner.
es: Ella va a preparar la cena.
note: Preparar la cena means to make or prepare dinner. Va a gives it a future meaning.

en: We're going to leave early.
note: Salir stays in the infinitive after vamos a. Temprano means early.

en: I'm going to take a shower.
note: With ducharse, me can go before voy or attach to the infinitive: voy a ducharme.

en: He's going to get up at six.
es: Él se va a levantar a las seis.
note: Levantarse uses se with él. A las seis gives the time he plans to get up.

en: We're going to see a movie.
note: Ver means to see or watch. Keep the a in vamos a ver.

en: I'm going to send a message.
note: Mandar un mensaje means to send a message. Voy a places it in the future.

en: You're going to need help. (one person)
note: Vas addresses one person informally. Necesitar stays in the infinitive.

en: They're going to move next year.
es: Ellos se van a mudar el próximo año.
note: Mudarse means to move home. Se goes before van, or attaches in van a mudarse.

en: I'm going to look for a job.
note: Buscar trabajo means to look for a job. No extra word for for is needed after buscar.

en: We're going to visit my parents.
es: Vamos a visitar a mis padres.
note: Keep both a's: vamos a introduces the future; a mis padres marks specific people.

en: She's going to bring dessert.
es: Ella va a traer el postre.
note: Traer stays in the infinitive after va a. El postre means dessert.

en: It's going to rain this afternoon.
note: Llover is a weather verb, so there is no personal subject. Use va a llover.

en: There's going to be a party.
note: The future of hay can be va a haber. Keep the a between va and haber.

en: I'm going to be late.
note: Llegar tarde literally means to arrive late and is a natural way to say be late.

en: You're going to have time to eat. (plural)
es: Ustedes van a tener tiempo para comer.
note: Ustedes takes van. Para comer explains what the time is for.

en: We're going to talk after lunch.
es: Vamos a hablar después del almuerzo.
note: Después de means after. De + el contracts to del.

en: I'm going to try again.
note: Otra vez means again. Intentar stays unchanged after voy a.

en: Are you going to pay by card? (one person)
note: Con tarjeta means by card. Vas identifies informal singular you.

en: He isn't going to be able to come.
es: Él no va a poder venir.
note: Va a gives the future; poder adds ability; venir stays in the infinitive after poder.

en: We're going to have to wait.
note: Combine future vamos a with obligation tener que, then the action esperar.

en: I'm going to tell her the truth.
es: Le voy a decir la verdad a ella.
note: Le is the recipient. A ella makes her explicit; le can also attach in voy a decirle.

en: They're going to get married in June.
es: Ellos se van a casar en junio.
note: Casarse means to get married. Use en before a month.

en: I'll call you later. (one person)
note: Simple future: add -é to the infinitive llamar for yo. Te identifies the person I will call.

en: You'll understand later. (one person)
note: Simple future: infinitive entender + -ás with tú. It keeps e here, unlike present entiendes.

en: She'll be here at five.
es: Ella estará aquí a las cinco.
note: Simple future: estar + -á with ella. Estar describes her location.

en: We'll talk tomorrow.
note: Simple future: hablar + -emos with nosotros. Hablaremos already identifies we.

en: They'll arrive on Monday.
note: Simple future: llegar + -án with ellos. El lunes gives the day.

en: You'll receive a message. (plural)
note: The simple future uses -án with ustedes, just as with ellos.

en: I'll be back soon.
note: Volver keeps its full infinitive in the future: volver + -é. It does not change to ue here.

en: I'll do it tomorrow.
note: Hacer has the irregular future stem har-. Lo stands for the thing I will do.

en: We'll have more time next week.
es: Tendremos más tiempo la próxima semana.
note: Tener uses the irregular future stem tendr-, then -emos for we.

en: I'll be able to help tomorrow.
note: Poder uses the irregular future stem podr-. Follow it with the infinitive ayudar.

en: He'll tell us what happened.
note: Decir uses the irregular future stem dir-. Nos means to us; qué pasó means what happened.

en: We'll know more tomorrow.
note: Saber uses the irregular future stem sabr-. Sabremos means we will know.

en: Everything will be fine.
note: Estará is the simple future of estar for a singular subject. Todo means everything.

en: There will be more opportunities.
note: Impersonal haber stays singular: habrá, even with plural oportunidades.

en: I'll go with you. (one person)
note: Ir forms its simple future by adding -é: iré. Contigo means with you, addressing tú.
